item.title: Judge says Trump can't demolish Kennedy Center. And, lawsuits target voter intimidation
item.description: A federal judge ruled yesterday that President Trump cannot tear down the Kennedy Center without a 30-day notice. And, recent lawsuits seek to keep armed federal officers away from polling sites.
item.content:encoded:
A federal judge ruled yesterday that President Trump cannot tear down the Kennedy Center without a 30-day notice. And, recent lawsuits seek to keep armed federal officers away from polling sites.

(Image credit: Kent Nishimura)

item.title: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman
item.description: Warren Buffett is stepping down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway after serving in the role for more than 50 years. His son, Howard, will become Berkshire Hathaway's new chairman

item.title: South Africa 'feels like a prison' for women amid spate of femicides
item.description: South Africa has some of the highest rates of violence against women in the world, and a spate of killings of nine women in the same area in recent weeks has led to renewed outrage.

item.title: Could trees developed with gene-editing technology protect Florida's citrus industry?
item.description: A bacterial infection is wiping out Florida's citrus trees. Growers hope a rootstock developed with gene-editing technology could keep the disease at bay.

item.title: Republican 'cavalry' arrives with a Trump-backed $150 million ad blitz in key races
item.description: To counter a difficult political environment, two Trump-aligned super PACs have reserved more than $150 million in ads — primarily in deep red House and Senate races that have now become competitive.

item.title: A DHS email raises new questions about the Trump administration's election plans
item.description: A heavily redacted email from last year, reported first by NPR, reveals that DHS personnel shared a list of jurisdictions that offer election materials in non-English languages. It's unclear why.
